correctness.rationale: For cover-supported elements of finite rooted-tree incidence algebras the unique path formula proves all powers have disjoint support among distinct rows. Therefore each power rank is exactly the count of vertices with maximal open downward path at least k. The polynomials mark these vertex path lengths and count each labeled edge assignment with exactly q-1 nonzero choices, hence enumerate all Jordan types. The max-index law follows a standard binomial Galton-Watson recurrence; the binary critical decay follows reciprocal increments, and deficit tightness follows uniform union and independent-subtree bounds. Literal exhaustive incidence-matrix and independently implemented multivariate polynomial tests pass for the listed finite cases; the full-radical conclusion is restricted to X^h only.

originality.rationale: A directly proved all-powers rank lemma and multivariate positive coefficient recurrence give every Jordan partition of the cover-supported canonical incidence action for all b,h and finite fields. The 2015 tree-percolation paper gives scalar root-to-leaf survival and criticality, which are explicitly prior work; it does not state the every-vertex all-powers Jordan spectrum. The 2026 layered-incidence result gives a top-power census only for ordinal sums of antichains, which do not include ancestry trees of depth two or more. published-finding corpus and accessible-own-ledger searches found no covering assertion. This is qualified because a general weighted-tree-shift theorem might imply it.
residual_risks: The polynomial recurrence may be implied by an unlocated general weighted-tree-shift Jordan-partition theorem.
The asymptotic branching threshold and scalar top-index survival are classical and not claimed independently new.
The search is bounded and cannot establish global publication priority.

value.rationale: Complete all-power Jordan type and exact finite-field multiplicity is a natural and previously unaccounted invariant for an unbounded basic family of incidence algebra radical elements, not a one-off parameter slice. The proof exposes a disjoint-row structural mechanism not reflected by scalar connectivity, and the maximal Jordan block shows a genuine field-order threshold with sharp logarithmic versus tight gap. The pre-existing scalar tree-percolation results are acknowledged as ingredients, not counted as the new contribution.
